title: A finite completely decomposed etale family descends to a finite stage
statement: Let $(R_\alpha)_\alpha$ be a directed system of commutative Noetherian rings with Noetherian direct limit $R$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and set $S_\alpha=\operatorname{Spec}R_\alpha$ and $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Fix $\alpha_0$, a finite type $S_{\alpha_0}$-scheme $P_{\alpha_0}$, and finitely many morphisms $v_{j,\alpha_0}:V_{j,\alpha_0}\to P_{\alpha_0}$, with every $V_{j,\alpha_0}$ of finite type over $S_{\alpha_0}$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Write $P_\alpha,V_{j,\alpha},v_{j,\alpha}$ and $P,V_j,v_j$ for their base changes [def-pc-fibre-product] to $S_\alpha$ and $S$. Assume that each $v_j$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] and that the family is completely decomposed: for every $p\in P$ there are $j$ and $z\in V_j$ above $p$ such that the canonical residue field map $\kappa(p)\to\kappa(z)$ is an isomorphism [def-weil-residue-field]. Then there is $\alpha_1\geq\alpha_0$ such that for every $\alpha\geq\alpha_1$, every $v_{j,\alpha}$ is etale and the family $(v_{j,\alpha})_j$ is completely decomposed. The assertion includes empty schemes and an empty family when its target is empty.

source.place: Expose III Lemma 3.1.1 and its proof by a finite closed filtration with sections on successive differences, printed p.38; the same argument applies to a finite family by taking its disjoint union. The rings and models here are Noetherian as in that lemma.
